audit_anchors_body: Each night the newest checkpoint of this log is witnessed by an independent service outside this server. Once a checkpoint is anchored, not even the operator can quietly rewrite the history before it.
audit_anchors_empty_body: The first checkpoint is written overnight, then anchored about half an hour later.
audit_anchors_howto: Anyone can check a proof offline, without contacting this server, with the time-stamp authority's certificate:
audit_anchors_off_body: Checkpoints are still signed and the chain can still be verified, but nothing outside this server has witnessed them.
audit_anchors_off_operator: The server's operator can turn it on with a time-stamp authority, a transparency log or both (AUDIT_ANCHOR_DRIVERS). Ask them if your auditors need it.
audit_anchors_off_title: External anchoring is not set up on this server
audit_anchors_pending_note: A new checkpoint waits for the next nightly run. If a service is unreachable, the run retries it for 7 days. A checkpoint is marked Failed when its retries run out, or when it could not be anchored at all because it failed its own checks; run Verify chain to see why. Only an RFC 3161 time-stamp proves when a checkpoint existed; a transparency-log entry proves it is in a public, append-only log.

audit_anchors_proof_named: Download the anchor proof for the checkpoint up to event {seq}

audit_subtitle: Every change in this workspace, who made it and when, in a tamper-evident chain.
audit_verify_anchors_late_note: Some checkpoints were first time-stamped more than 8 days after they were written. They prove the history existed from that time on, not from when it happened.
audit_verify_anchors_missing_note: Some checkpoints older than 8 days have no receipt. Ask the server's operator to check the anchoring job.

audit_verify_anchors_unverified_note: Some receipts are intact but signed by a service this server does not pin. They still show the checkpoint existed, but not who said so.
audit_verify_body: Recomputes every event's hash and checks it against the one before it. Any edit or deletion breaks the chain.

dataroom_failed_body: The preview could not be generated. Download it if downloads are allowed.
dataroom_forensic_body: Who was served a forensically marked copy of this document, and a test that traces a leaked page image back to one of them.
dataroom_forensic_error_not_found: That page or version of this document doesn't exist. Check the page number and version.
dataroom_forensic_explain_evidence: A match is evidence of whose copy the image came from, not proof of who leaked it: someone else may have used their screen, device or account.
dataroom_forensic_explain_inconclusive: A lower band is inconclusive: it is not evidence on its own. Try a sharper, larger or less cropped image of the same page. The thresholds this test used are shown with the result.
dataroom_forensic_explain_match: Each recipient gets a score. A match needs a score above a threshold that rises with the number of recipients tested, so that in any one test the chance of naming an innocent recipient as a match stays below about one in a million.
dataroom_forensic_explain_privacy: The image is used for this one test and is not stored. The test itself is recorded in the audit log.
dataroom_forensic_image_hint: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to {max} MB, at least 200 pixels wide. One page, as uncropped as you have it.
dataroom_forensic_image_too_large: That image is larger than {max} MB.
dataroom_forensic_image_type: That isn't a PNG, JPEG or WebP image.
dataroom_forensic_off_note: Forensic watermarking is off for this document. Only pages served while it was on carry a mark.

match.countPlural=one: The page the image shows. This version has {count} page.
match.countPlural=*: The page the image shows. This version has {count} pages.

dataroom_forensic_page_invalid: Enter a whole page number, 1 or more.
dataroom_forensic_recipients_empty_body: Recipients appear here the first time they open a page while forensic watermarking is on.
dataroom_forensic_result_inconclusive_no: No recipient scored as a match. Inconclusive scores are not evidence on their own: try a better image of the same page.

match.countPlural=one: {count} recipient couldn't be tested: the key their mark was made with has since been retired from this server.
match.countPlural=*: {count} recipients couldn't be tested: the key their marks were made with has since been retired from this server.

dataroom_forensic_result_match_note: The image carries the mark of the recipient marked Match. Treat it as evidence to follow up, not as a conclusion.
dataroom_forensic_result_none_body: Nobody who was served this version scored as a match or inconclusive. That does not rule anyone out: the image may come from another version or page, may be too degraded, or may have been altered.
dataroom_forensic_result_tamper_body: At least one recipient's mark shows up inverted, which happens when copies are averaged or a mark is deliberately subtracted. Treat every score from this image with caution, and keep the original file.
dataroom_forensic_result_tamper_title: This image may have been tampered with
dataroom_forensic_trace_body: Upload a screenshot or photo of one page that turned up somewhere it shouldn't have. We test it against the invisible mark of everyone who was served that version.
dataroom_forensic_trace_code_note: A leaked download carries a line reading “trace” and an 8-character code. Find that code in the Download trace column to see whose copy it was.
dataroom_forensic_trace_pending: Testing the image against every marked copy. This can take a few seconds.
dataroom_forensic_version_hint: The version the image was taken from, if you know it.
dataroom_forensic_view_as_note: Also served under view-as: this staff member opened this version at least once while viewing the portal as an investor. Those pages carried the staff member's own mark, never the investor's. It does not say whether a given copy, or the leaked one, was a view-as copy.

domains_added: Domain added. Publish both records, then verify.
domains_driver_manual: This install verifies who owns a hostname and nothing more: your own proxy terminates TLS, so no certificate is issued here.
domains_error_canonical_host: That is this portal's own address. It already works — there is nothing to add.
domains_error_canonical_subdomain: That hostname already belongs to this install. Use one on a domain you own.
domains_error_claimed_elsewhere: Another workspace on this install has already verified that hostname. It has to be released there before it can be verified here.
domains_error_duplicate: That hostname is already on this list.
domains_error_ip_literal: That is an IP address. Point a hostname at it and add the hostname instead.
domains_error_not_a_hostname: That is not a hostname. Letters, digits and hyphens separated by dots — no scheme, no port, no path.
domains_error_public_suffix: Nobody owns that name on its own. Use a hostname underneath it.
domains_error_reserved: That name is reserved for local networks, so no certificate can ever be issued for it.
domains_error_too_long: That hostname is too long for DNS.
domains_error_wildcard: Wildcards are not supported. Add each hostname you want to serve.
domains_error_workspace_already_verified: This workspace already has a verified domain. Remove it first: one portal keeps one hostname, because a session on one hostname cannot follow an investor to another.
This workspace already serves {host}. Remove that first: one portal keeps one hostname, because a session on one hostname cannot follow an investor to another.
domains_field_help: A subdomain such as investors.yourcompany.com. An apex domain works only if your DNS provider offers ALIAS, ANAME or CNAME flattening.
domains_none_body: Investors reach this portal on the address it came with. A custom domain replaces that address; it changes nothing else.
domains_provider_records_body: Cloudflare validates on its own through the CNAME above. If you cannot wait for that, or your DNS blocks it, publishing these records as well lets Cloudflare validate directly.
domains_remove_body: The portal stops answering on that hostname within a minute, and everyone signed in there is signed out: a session cookie belongs to one hostname and cannot be moved to another. Links already emailed keep pointing at it.
domains_sending_note: Sending email from your own domain is a different record set with its own verification.
domains_state_active: Serving. This is the workspace's primary origin now, so emailed links point here.
domains_state_dns_ok: Both records resolve, so a certificate is now allowed — but none exists yet. It is obtained on the first HTTPS request to the hostname, so open it once: that load takes a second or two, and every load after it is instant.
domains_state_dns_ok_provider: Both records resolve, and Cloudflare has been asked to issue the certificate. There is nothing more to do: this domain goes live by itself as soon as Cloudflare reports the hostname and its certificate active — usually within minutes, occasionally a few hours.
domains_state_failed: Nothing resolved for 72 hours, so we stopped looking. Fix the records and verify to start again.
domains_state_pending: Publish both records, then verify. We also re-check every five minutes on our own, and give up on {deadline}.
domains_subtitle: Serve this portal from a hostname you own, such as investors.yourcompany.com.
domains_verify_not_yet: Not there yet. DNS changes take a while, and two resolvers have to agree before anything counts as verified.
domains_verify_ok: Both records resolve. Open the domain over HTTPS to get its certificate.

embed_frame_ancestors_body: Derived from the list above every time this screen loads, so it cannot disagree with what the browser is actually sent. 'self' is always there, which is what lets the portal preview its own embed.
embed_handoff_body: Let your own website tell this portal who its visitor is, so an investor already signed in on your site does not sign in again here.
embed_handoff_key_id_dup: A key with that ID is already registered. Remove it first, or pick another ID.
embed_handoff_key_id_invalid: Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, up to 64 characters. Your site chose this when it made the key.
embed_handoff_key_public_help: The public half only, base64url, 43 characters. Never paste the private half anywhere.
embed_handoff_key_public_invalid: That is not an Ed25519 public key. It should be 43 characters of base64url — letters, digits, dash and underscore.
embed_handoff_keys_full: At most {max} keys, which is enough to rotate one. Remove an old key first.
embed_handoff_keys_none: No key registered. Your site generates an Ed25519 key pair, keeps the private half and gives you the public half to paste here.
embed_handoff_off_body: Investors sign in here, inside the frame or in a window of their own. Turning this on trades that for convenience: a compromise of your website would become a way to sign in here as an investor you have already invited.
embed_handoff_off_title: Off: nobody can assert an identity to this portal
embed_handoff_on_body: Read that as what it is — if your website is compromised, whoever holds it can sign in here as any investor you have already invited. What bounds it: the assertion lasts 60 seconds, works once, cannot enrol anyone new, and buys the weakest session there is, so the data room and every other guarded action still asks for proof. Every use is in the audit log.
embed_handoff_on_title: On: your website can say who a visitor is
embed_handoff_toggle: Accept signed identity from my site
embed_handoff_toggle_hint: Off unless you have a reason. Your site needs a server that can sign an assertion.
embed_insecure_body: The portal can only run inside pages served over HTTPS. Open it in its own tab to continue.
embed_origin_error_duplicate: That origin is already on the list.
embed_origin_error_has_credentials: Drop the user name and password: an origin is scheme and host only.
embed_origin_error_has_path: That is a page address, not an origin. Keep the scheme and host and drop the rest: https://acme.com, not https://acme.com/investors.
embed_origin_error_insecure: Only https:// is accepted, except http://localhost and http://127.0.0.1 for local development. A browser will not keep a sign-in inside a frame on an http: page at all.
embed_origin_error_not_an_origin: That is not an origin. It should look like https://acme.com.
embed_origin_error_server: The server refused {origin}. It has to be an https:// origin with no path.
embed_origin_error_too_many: The list holds at most {max} origins. Remove one first.
embed_origin_error_wildcard: Wildcards are not accepted. https://*.acme.com trusts every host anyone can ever put under that domain, including a staging box you have forgotten about. List each origin instead.
embed_origin_field_help: Scheme and host, nothing else: https://acme.com. www. is a different origin, and so is a different port, so list each one. Wildcards are refused — the only wildcards in the product are the six builder-preview patterns behind the toggle below.
embed_origins_body: Only these sites may frame this portal. The list becomes a Content-Security-Policy header, which the browser enforces on our response before any of our code runs — there is no snippet option that gets round it.
embed_origins_none: No site can frame this portal yet, apart from the portal itself.
embed_preview_body: Website builders serve their preview from a shared address you cannot know until you publish. This toggle adds all six of them at once.
embed_preview_off_body: Turning this on would allow every site on all six, not only yours, because a builder's preview address is shared:
embed_preview_off_title: Off: these domains cannot frame this portal
embed_preview_on_body: Not only yours. Every Webflow, Framer, Wix and Squarespace site shares these addresses, so while this is on, any of them can put your portal in a page of their own. It is meant for the hour between building a page and publishing it.
embed_preview_on_title: On: any site on these domains can frame this portal
embed_preview_toggle_hint: Turn this off once your real origin is on the list above.
embed_settings_subtitle: Put this portal inside your own website. Add the origins allowed to frame it, then paste one of the snippets below.
embed_snippet_iframe_hint: For pages that allow an iframe but no script. You give up the automatic height, deep links and the link fallback. Do not change referrerpolicy to no-referrer: it is the only signal that tells this portal who framed it.
embed_snippet_loader_hint: Use this one wherever you can run a script. The loader sizes the frame to its content, keeps a deep link in the page address, and falls back to a plain link if anything goes wrong. It updates itself: fixes reach a snippet nobody ever edits again.
embed_snippet_pinned_hint: The same loader, frozen at one version whose bytes the browser verifies. Use it when a security review asks for it, or when your site's policy is integrity-based. The cost is that you now own the upgrade: nothing about this URL will ever change, including its bugs.
embed_snippets_body: Paste one of these into the page that should show the portal. Neither will render until the page's origin is on the list above.

erasure_retained: Kept on purpose: consent history, document acceptances, audit records and round commitments (evidence and legal obligation).

esign_rejected_title: The vendor did not accept the connection

esign_rotate_secret_body: The current secret stops working at once. Until you paste the new one into {vendor}, callbacks are refused and status updates arrive only through the periodic check.

esign_setup_documenso_1: In Documenso, open Settings → Webhooks and create a webhook with the callback URL.
esign_setup_documenso_2: Subscribe it to the document signed, completed, rejected and cancelled events.
esign_setup_documenso_3: Paste the callback secret this page showed you into the webhook's Secret field.
esign_setup_docuseal_1: In DocuSeal, open Settings → Webhooks and add the callback URL.
esign_setup_docuseal_2: Add a custom header named X-Fundroom-Signature whose value is the callback secret this page showed you. A connection set up with the old X-Seedhost-Signature header keeps working; rename the header when you next rotate the secret.
esign_setup_docuseal_3: Select the form and submission events.
esign_setup_docuseal_note: Signing NDAs sends a PDF, which needs DocuSeal Cloud or DocuSeal Pro. The open-source edition can only send template documents (round closing).
esign_setup_docusign_1: In DocuSign eSignature Admin, open Connect and add a custom configuration for the whole account, with the callback URL as its URL.
esign_setup_docusign_2: Turn on “Include HMAC signature”, generate a key, and paste it into the Connect HMAC key field on this page. The key is DocuSign's: this workspace has no secret of its own to give you.
esign_setup_docusign_3: Select the envelope events sent, delivered, completed, declined and voided.
esign_setup_docusign_note: To rotate the HMAC key, add the new key as the secondary key here first, then switch DocuSign over, then move it to the main field.
esign_setup_dropbox_sign_1: In Dropbox Sign, open API settings and set the account callback URL to the callback URL.
esign_setup_dropbox_sign_2: There is no separate secret: Dropbox Sign signs its callbacks with your API key.
esign_setup_dropbox_sign_note: Dropbox Sign cannot be signed inside this portal: signers always receive their signing link by email.
esign_sign_page_done_body: Your signature is recorded. If you started from another window, you can close this one.
esign_sign_page_empty_body: There is no agreement for you to sign here. If you followed a link, it may already be signed or no longer current.

esign_void_failed: The envelope could not be voided
export_contents_audit: The audit trail, with its hash chain and checkpoints, so it can be checked after the move.
export_contents_body: One zip file with everything this workspace holds, in open formats (JSON Lines and the original files), to move to another FundRoom instance or keep as an archive.
export_contents_files: Every uploaded file — data-room documents, logos, attachments — decrypted, exactly as it was uploaded.
export_contents_manifest: A manifest listing every file with its checksum, signed with this instance's export key.
export_contents_not: Not included: passwords, passkeys, sessions, API tokens and other secrets; people re-verify their email on the new instance.
export_contents_tables: Every record: people and groups, access grants, content, updates, metrics, the round, CRM, legal documents and acceptances.
export_copy_sha256: Copy SHA-256 of the export from {date}
export_delete_body: The export from {date} is deleted from storage now. A copy that was already downloaded is not affected.
export_downloaded: Your browser is saving {file}. Its downloads list shows the progress.
export_downloaded_sha_hint: When the download finishes, compare this with the SHA-256 of the saved file (for example, shasum -a 256 {file}). If they differ, the file is incomplete or was altered: download it again.
export_forbidden: Only the workspace owner can export the workspace.
export_keys_body: Every export is signed. Whoever imports it can check the signature against this public key, so share the key through a channel other than the file itself.
export_list_body: Exports are prepared in the background and kept for 7 days, then deleted. Downloading asks you to confirm it is you.
export_plaintext_body: The zip contains every document and record in plaintext, without the encryption that protects them here. Store it, send it and delete it with the same care as the originals.
export_plaintext_title: Handle the file like the originals
export_raw_analytics_hint: Every individual page and document view, not only the totals. Makes the file larger and holds more personal data.
export_request_body: Starting an export asks you to confirm it is you. Only one export can be prepared at a time.
export_requested: Export started. It appears below when it is ready.
export_subtitle: Download everything in this workspace as one signed file.
export_verify_body: Check an export before importing it anywhere: the command verifies the signature and every checksum.
group_add_members_body: Pick people to add. Access from the group's grants applies right away.

legal_documents_subtitle: This workspace's own texts. Each published version is immutable and carries the hash of the exact bytes investors were shown.

legal_field_requires_acceptance: Investors must accept this before entering the portal
legal_field_template_hint: Templates are a starting point, not a finished document.
legal_field_warning_days_hint: Under Rule 506(b), flag an investor given access within this many days of the relationship being established. It warns; it never blocks.
legal_metadata_subtitle: Who sees it, and whether it has to be accepted.

legal_not_advice_body: FundRoom cannot tell you which exemption your raise relies on. Have your counsel confirm the mode before you change it.
legal_publish_counsel_body: You are about to put a legal text in front of investors, and it will be recorded as the exact wording they agreed to. FundRoom does not review it. Have your counsel read it first.
legal_publish_subtitle: Versions are immutable. Publishing writes a new one and asks everyone who must accept it to accept it again.
legal_publish_unchanged: The text is unchanged, so no new version was published
legal_region_will_suggest: When you save, the consent mode changes to this region's suggested default. Choose a mode yourself to keep it instead.
legal_register_empty: Nobody has accepted this document yet.

legal_versions_subtitle: Each row is a text that was in force. They cannot be edited or deleted.

mail_forbidden: Only workspace owners and admins can see mail delivery settings.
mail_hint_generic: Paste the webhook URL above into your provider's delivery-event settings.
mail_hint_no_webhooks: Delivery webhooks are not configured on this server, so bounces and complaints are not recorded and nothing is suppressed automatically. Ask whoever runs the server to set the provider's webhook secret.
mail_hint_postmark: In Postmark, open your server's Webhooks, add the URL above with the webhook user and password (POSTMARK_WEBHOOK_USER and POSTMARK_WEBHOOK_PASSWORD) as basic-auth credentials, and turn on Delivery, Bounce, Spam complaint, Open and Click. Do this for the broadcast stream too.
mail_hint_resend: In Resend, open Webhooks, add the URL above and subscribe to email.delivered, email.bounced, email.complained, email.delivery_delayed, email.opened and email.clicked. The signing secret goes in RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET on the server.
mail_hint_ses: Point your SES configuration set's event destination at an SNS topic, subscribe the URL above to that topic over HTTPS, and list the topic ARN in SES_SNS_TOPIC_ARNS on the server. The subscription is confirmed automatically.
mail_hint_smtp: SMTP has no delivery webhooks: bounces come back as ordinary mail, so nothing is recorded or suppressed automatically. Switch to Resend, Postmark or Amazon SES to get bounce and complaint handling.
mail_status_body: The mail service this server sends with, and where it reports what happened to each message.
mail_subtitle: How email leaves this workspace, and who it has stopped writing to.
mail_suppressions_body: Hard bounces and spam complaints stop update and notification emails to that address. Sign-in and invitation emails are never held back. Addresses are shown masked: only a keyed fingerprint of each one is stored.
mail_tracking_account_hint: This provider switches open and click tracking on or off for the whole account, not per message. Events from members who have not agreed to email tracking are discarded when they arrive.
mail_unsuppress_body: Update and notification emails will go to this address again. If the provider reports another hard bounce or spam complaint, it is suppressed again.

platform_cells_none_body: This install has not recorded any cell yet.

platform_create_country_invalid: Choose the country the company is registered in.

platform_decision_cleared_toast: Cleared. The workspace can be used again.
